chunks: From him, from his father, from Abu Nahshal, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'From the respect of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the respect for the believer with gray hair (old age); and whoever honors a believer, he has begun by honoring Allah, and whoever treats lightly a believer with gray hair, Allah will send to him one who will treat him lightly before his death.'

key_terms.إِجْلَالُ: Respect, veneration, or honoring with reverence
key_terms.اسْتَخَفَّ: To treat lightly, to belittle, or to show disrespect
key_terms.ذِي الشَّيْبَةِ: The one with gray hair, referring to an elderly person

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of respecting elderly believers in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the physical dignity of the elderly believer directly to the majesty of Allah, establishing a theological hierarchy where honoring the creation honors the Creator. This tradition underscores the Shia emphasis on 'Ijlaal' (reverence) as a spiritual discipline, warning that slighting the aged invites divine retribution through a reciprocal slighter, thereby preserving social and cosmic order.
